## Model boundaries {#lifecycle-authority}

Structured `couple_inductive()` accepts a fixed Quantity; coupling-coefficient
parameter binding and optimization are not supported. The
[component contract](../component-authoring.qmd) defines the physical models,
and the [Parameter System](parameter-system.qmd) defines which inputs may vary.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Electrical resolution

### Policy and realized mesh {#electrical-resolution-candidate-converging}

`ElectricalResolution(max_frequency=10*u.GHz,
sections_per_wavelength=40)` is an immutable, per-line alternative to
`n_sections`; exactly one must be supplied. It is available only for a line
whose declared R and G matrices are explicitly and exactly zero. The Plan
owns this policy and physical line lengths, while each bound candidate owns
its realized integer grids. Rebinding length may change a grid, but it never
changes conductor order, line connectivity, public Pins, or Port identities.

`run.explain()` and verified numerical Results expose the realized line
inventory in declaration order. Each record provides physical length, N,
and dx; policy records additionally provide modal velocities and hmax with
units. Point outcomes and checkpoints retain their own grids, as do the
Optimization baseline, evaluated candidates, and best point. Fixed-count
lines report their actual N and dx without a fictional modal calculation.
Missing or nonzero R/G, invalid policy inputs, invalid modal matrices, and
non-finite or unrepresentable sections fail closed; the existing fixed-count
lossy path remains available. A complex root above the saved policy's
`|ω|/(2π)` envelope is visibly identified, not rejected or remeshed.
Neither the policy nor any reported refinement difference is an observable
error bound. The [concept](../concepts/electrical-resolution.qmd) and
[compiler implementation](../implementation/rlgc-q2d-and-pi-expansion.qmd)
give the derivation and realization mechanics.

:::
